items.title: Amazon S3 Vectors metadata pre-filtering is now available in AWS GovCloud (US) Regions

items.content_snippet: See how the Codex community brings people together to build, learn, and share. Pauline Narvas and VB talk about growing the Codex Ambassador program, their favorite moments from local meetups and Build Week, and what it means to build with heart.

items.title: How Oracle Uses ChatGPT Work to Transform Recruitment
items.content_snippet: “We’ve gone from zero to 100, not zero to 60.” Jan Ackerman shares how Oracle built a talent market intelligence tool with ChatGPT Work to transform hiring preparation. Starting with a job description, it researches comparable roles, benchmarks compensation, and assesses talent pools across locations, giving hiring managers consistent data and insights. Read how Oracle is transforming work with ChatGPT Work and Codex: https://openai.com/index/oracle/

items.content_snippet: Slop isn't AI-written code. It's work that looks finished before the thinking is. Gabriel "Gabo" Martinez, engineering manager and self-described slop warden at G2i, explains what slop really is: what happens when generation outruns judgment, when ambiguity gets cleared with guesses and nobody notices there was a choice to make. items.title: From Context to Memory: Your Agents Need a Real Memory Layer — Anders Swanson, Oracle
items.content_snippet: Your agent rereads the same files every session because nothing it learned was saved. Anders Swanson, developer evangelist for Oracle Database, treats agent memory as a systems problem. Context windows aren't memory, bigger windows aren't the fix, and markdown scratch pads and grep don't scale. Keep going down that road and you'll end up building your own database. He walks through the pattern modern memory systems are converging on: formation, recall, evolution and evaluation, plus governance.
